title: Divisorial charts of a smooth strict normal crossings pair
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field and $f:V\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ a smooth finite-type morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Z$ be a reduced effective Cartier divisor on $V$ whose finitely many irreducible components are smooth and meet transversely, i.e. $Z$ is a smooth strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. Let $U=V\setminus |Z|$ be the canonical open complement of $Z\hookrightarrow V$. Then $U\to V$ has dense range and the divisorial pair $(V,U)$ is a fine-saturated log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. For every geometric point $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$, there are an integer $r\ge0$, a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$, and a chart $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf N^r)\to M(W)$ whose stalk map is a chart for the divisorial stalk. The chart monoid is fine saturated and its characteristic monoid is isomorphic to $\mathbf N^r$. The images of the standard basis are part of a regular system of parameters of the strict local ring $A=\mathcal O_{V,\bar v}$; the quotient by the ideal they generate is regular and $\dim A=\dim A/(t_1,\ldots,t_r)+r$. The empty divisor is allowed (the case $r=0$).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over the field $F$ to see that $V$ is Noetherian. For any point $p$ of $V$ or of one of the given smooth intersections, [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-smooth-field-criterion], with the field extension $F/F$, makes its ordinary local ring regular. For a geometric point over $p$, [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison], applied to an affine open containing $p$, identifies the strict local ring (the pointed-neighbourhood colimit) with an algebraic strict henselization of the ordinary local ring relative to the separable closure of $\kappa(p)$ in $\Omega$, compatibly with the maps from the affine coordinate ring. That strict henselization is regular by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular]. Thus both ordinary and strict local rings used below are Noetherian regular local rings. For each smooth codimension-one component $Z_i\hookrightarrow V$, use the codimension-one case of [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] to obtain a local equation $t_i$ generating its ideal and a nonzerodivisor. These are separate applications to individual components, not simultaneous coordinate choices. Around a fixed geometric point $\bar v$ on $r$ components, take a common open neighbourhood $W$ for these finitely many equations, and remove all components not through $\bar v$. On $W$ the complement $U$ of $|Z|$ is $D(T)$, where $T=t_1\cdots t_r$ (empty product $1$).

proof.text: Fix any point $p\in W$ and let $J=\{i:t_i(p)=0\}$, $s=|J|$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{W,p}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, residue field $\kappa$, and $d=\dim R$. The scheme-theoretic intersection $Y_J$ has local ring $R/I$, where $I=(t_i:i\in J)$, and it is regular by Step 1. The smooth codimension-$s$ hypothesis says that the local topological dimensions of $W$ and $Y_J$ at $p$ differ by $s$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] to affine neighbourhoods in both schemes: their residue fields at $p$ agree, so subtracting the identical transcendence-degree terms gives $\dim(R/I)=d-s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], the natural surjection $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to(\mathfrak m/I)/(\mathfrak m/I)^2$ has kernel $(I+\mathfrak m^2)/\mathfrak m^2$ of dimension $s$. The $s$ classes of the specified $t_i$ span this kernel because they generate $I$; they are therefore linearly independent. Extend them to a $\kappa$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, and lift the remaining basis vectors to $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] the resulting $d$ elements generate $\mathfrak m$, hence form a regular system of parameters. This proves the simultaneous assertion for the actual component equations. For $J=\varnothing$, $I=0$ and the argument just chooses a parameter system of $R$.

proof.text: At a geometric point $\bar w$ over $p$, let $A$ be the strict local ring; by [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] it is, as an algebra over the affine coordinate ring, an algebraic strict henselization $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of $R$, so the chosen elements of the coordinate ring have the same images in both. The canonical cotangent isomorphism of [lem-sc-strict-henselization-cotangent-dimension] takes the basis just chosen to a basis after extending the residue field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to the maximal ideal of the Noetherian local ring $A$. Those same $d$ elements generate it. Since $A$ is regular by Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] gives $\dim A=d$. Thus $(t_i:i\in J)$ is part of a regular system of parameters of $A$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] yields that $A/(t_i:i\in J)$ is regular of dimension $\dim A-s$. This argument applies at every $\bar w$ of $W$, with its own set $J$, rather than assuming a fixed number of components through all points.

proof.text: Use the stalk and divisorial definitions [def-trf-log-regular-pair, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. At $\bar w$, the inclusion $M\subset\mathcal O_W$ identifies $M_{\bar w}$ with precisely $\{f\in A:f\text{ is a unit in }A[1/T]\}$. Indeed a germ of a divisorial section has an affine pointed etale representative $\operatorname{Spec}B\to W$; its inverse on $D(T)\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$ gives an inverse in $B[1/T]$ and hence in $A[1/T]$. Conversely represent $f\in A$ at such a neighbourhood. If $f$ is invertible in $A[1/T]$, there are $g\in A$ and $n\ge0$ with $fg=T^n$: a localization inverse gives this after multiplication by a power of $T$. The elements and this one equality descend to a common pointed etale neighbourhood, since $A$ is its ring colimit. There $f$ is invertible on $D(T)$, so represents a section of $M$. Equality of two such germs in $A$ likewise means equality after refinement; thus this identification is injective as well. The same finite inverse equation shows that the stalk of $\mathcal O_W^\times$ is $A^\times$.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.4, printed p. 69; explicit finite-witness calculation of its divisorial stalk.

proof.text: The sections $t_i$ define $\alpha:P=\mathbf N^r\to M(W)$. At $\bar w$ put $K=\{1,\ldots,r\}\setminus J$. The $t_i$ for $i\in K$ are units in $A$; those for $i\in J$ form part of a parameter system by Step 3. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] to $A$ and the latter tuple. Step 4 then gives $M_{\bar w}=\{u\prod_{i\in J}t_i^{a_i}:u\in A^\times,\ a_i\ge0\}$. The parameters are pairwise nonassociate: association would make two of their cotangent basis vectors proportional. Unique factorization makes this expression unique, including the unit coefficient. Since a product in a commutative ring is a unit only if each factor is a unit, $\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)=\mathbf N^K$. In the chart pushout, absorb each unit coordinate into the coefficient: $(n,u)\mapsto(n|_J,u\prod_{i\in K}t_i^{n_i})$. This identifies $P\oplus_{\mathbf N^K}A^\times$ with $\mathbf N^J\oplus A^\times$, and the displayed unique expression identifies the latter with $M_{\bar w}$. This proves the full pushout condition of [def-trf-log-regular-pair] at every point of the one chart. Consequently $\overline M_{\bar w}\cong\mathbf N^J$; only at the chosen centre is $J=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and its rank $r$.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1, 1.4 and 1.5(i), printed pp. 69–70; the local factorization input is more-algebra.tex Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD.

proof.text: For $J=\{i:t_i(p)=0\}$, a monomial in Step 5 is a nonunit exactly when at least one exponent with index in $J$ is positive. Thus the ideal generated by all images of nonunits of $M_{\bar w}$ is exactly $I_{\bar w}=(t_i:i\in J)$: every nonunit is divisible by one such $t_i$, and each such $t_i$ is itself a nonunit section. Step 3 supplies regularity of $A/I_{\bar w}$ and $\dim A=\dim(A/I_{\bar w})+|J|$. Step 5 gives group completion $\mathbf Z^J$, of rank $|J|$. This verifies precisely the quotient and dimension conditions of [def-trf-log-regular-pair], also when $J$ is empty.

The monoid $\mathbf N^r$ is generated by its basis, embeds in $\mathbf Z^r$, and is saturated there: if $na$ has every coordinate nonnegative for $n>0$, so does $a$. Hence the charts constructed above are fine saturated. Step 5 shows the log structure is trivial exactly where $J$ is empty, namely $U$. The open $U$ is dense: at each ordinary local ring, which is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], the local product of boundary parameters is nonzero and its distinguished open contains the generic point. This includes the empty-divisor case $T=1$. Together with Step 6, the definition [def-trf-log-regular-pair] proves log regularity. At $\bar v$ the parameter and quotient claims are Steps 2–3 and its characteristic is $\mathbf N^r$ by Step 5.

Step 2 shows the actual component equations form part of a regular system of parameters: the dimension formula gives dim R/I = d−s, so their cotangent classes are independent, and Nakayama lifts an extended basis. Step 3 passes this to the strict local ring through the cotangent isomorphism, Nakayama and the regular-sequence lemma. Step 4 identifies the divisorial stalk by one finite inverse equation. Step 5 builds the pushout chart at each point with characteristic N^J; Steps 6 and 7 cover the ideal, rank, fs, triviality locus and density. Edge cases checked: empty Z, dimension 0, one divisor, the axes in A^2 (ranks 2, 1, 0 from one chart) and nonclosed points. statement_change.old_statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field and $V$ a smooth finite-type $F$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Z\subset V$ be a reduced effective Cartier divisor [def-weil-closed-immersion], meaning locally one non-zero-divisor cuts it out, and assume that its finitely many irreducible components $Z_i$ are smooth and every intersection of $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth of codimension $r$ in $V$. The empty divisor is allowed. At any geometric point on exactly $r$ components, the divisorial log structure $M$ of $(V,|Z|)$ has an etale-local chart $\mathbf N^r\to M$ sending the standard basis to local equations $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ of those components. These equations form part of a regular system of parameters of the strict local ring $A$; its characteristic monoid is $\overline M_{\bar v}\cong\mathbf N^r$, and $A/(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ is regular of dimension $\dim A-r$. In particular $(V,|Z|)$ is a log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair].
statement_change.what: The source statement names the pair (V,|Z|) and a divisorial log structure but introduces neither the open complement U nor the scheme-theoretic morphism whose dense range and log-regular predicate are required by the recorded definition. It also leaves the local chart, characteristic, parameter, quotient, and dimension clauses without Lean objects. The correction uses the canonical open complement of Z.subschemeι, the existing smooth strict normal crossings divisor predicate, and explicit chart data matching ILO VI 1.4--1.5(i). The characteristic clause was then repaired after independent review: it now supplies a multiplicative equivalence from the actual stalk characteristic monoid `Associates (divisorialStalk ...)` to `Multiplicative (Fin r → ℕ)` and requires it to send every associated chart germ to the corresponding ULift coordinate, hence in particular every standard basis image and boundary parameter. The second independent return identified that the Lean parameter clause incorrectly asserted that the r boundary equations alone were a full regular system of parameters. For the empty divisor on the affine line at a closed geometric point, r = 0 while the strict local ring has dimension 1, so this was false. The repaired signature existentially supplies a remaining list s and asserts that the ordered boundary list concatenated with s is a regular system of parameters, exactly rendering the unchanged source phrase part of a regular system of parameters.
